title: Which built-in tool answers this question?
head: Question you are asking
Tool
Watch out for
rows: Which files have names like this?
Only paths are matched, never contents
Only as good as the text marker
Change one unique spot in a file
Rewrite a file, or Edit can't find a unique match
rule: Glob for names and paths, Grep for contents. Choose the one whose signal you can trust.

title: Edit failed: what is the next move?
head: What you observe
Where the fault is
Fix
rows: Match not unique, but nearby lines differ
Match not unique, surroundings identical everywhere
File changed since it was read
rule: Edit needs a unique text match. When the text can't be unique, Read the file and Write it back.

title: Exploring code: which way to look?
head: What you observe
Where the fault is
Fix
rows: Find who calls a function, then fix it here
Narrow trace; code needed in session
Grep for references, Read callers, follow imports
Broad survey; only conclusions needed, or context tight
Find files by name or extension
rule: Start from the entry point: Grep for references and Read outward. Delegate to Explore only when you need conclusions, not code.

title: Changing part of a file: which tool?
head: What you observe
Where the fault is
Fix
rows: Edit match ambiguous, but a unique anchor exists
Widen the match to the unique part
Read, then Write the whole file
Same change wanted at every match
rule: Ambiguous Edit match: widen it to something unique. Use Read + Write only when nothing is unique.

title: Finding your way in code: which tool, and who does it?
head: Situation
Right mechanism
Why
rows: Find where text appears, whatever the file name
Find files by name pattern (e.g. all tests)
Only the conclusion is wanted; discovery is verbose
Keeps noise out of the main context
rule: Search by content when names are unreliable, then read along the trail one file at a time. Delegate to Explore only when the trail itself isn't wanted.

title: Edit failed: what kind of failure is it?
head: What you observe
Where the fault is
Fix
rows: Match not unique, neighbouring lines differ
Match not unique, copies identical for many lines
Read the file, Write it back changed
Don't know where the text is
Change belongs in the source of generated code
Edit the generator, if every output should change
rule: Edit needs a unique text anchor. When none exists, Read the whole file and Write it back with the change.

title: Which built-in tool answers this question?
head: What you need
Tool
Why
rows: Every file that mentions a name or string
Every file whose path matches a pattern
Understand a flow from an entry point
Grep for entry, then Read along the calls
rule: Grep searches inside files. Glob matches file names and paths.

title: Changing a file: which built-in tool?
head: Situation
Tool
Why
rows: Text to change is unique in the file
Text to change appears several times
rule: Unique text: Edit. Not unique: Read, then Write.
